accepted.s: The Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign of January–February 1922 was associated with which administrative unit?
accepted.x: The campaign was conducted in the Pedanandipadu firka of Guntur district during January–February 1922.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise administrative unit instead of confusing a firka with a taluka or district.
accepted.sec: ■ Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign - firka, district, leaders, tax refused  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The tax refused by the peasants of Pedanandipadu firka was the:
accepted.x: The campaign involved refusal to pay the January instalment of land revenue.
accepted.tq: Test the exact revenue item and instalment rather than the broad idea of tax resistance.
accepted.sec: ■ Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign - firka, district, leaders, tax refused  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the resignation of village officers in the Pedanandipadu firka:
1. Eighteen out of nineteen village officers in the firka resigned.
2. Twenty-nine village officers resigned in Guntur district.
3. The resignations were led by Machiraju Ramamurthy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The mass resignation involved 18 of 19 officers in the firka, 29 in Guntur district, and was led by Chandavolu karanam Machiraju Ramamurthy.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical cluster and the associated leader to verify all statements.
accepted.sec: ■ Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign - firka, district, leaders, tax refused  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who led the Shanti Sena in the Pedanandipadu firka?
accepted.x: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary led the Shanti Sena in the firka and was also associated with the no-tax campaign.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the local organiser of the Shanti Sena from the leader of the village-officer resignations.
accepted.sec: ■ Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign - firka, district, leaders, tax refused  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The decision to form the Shanti Sena was taken by the Guntur District Congress Committee in:
accepted.x: The Guntur District Congress Committee decided to form the Shanti Sena in December 1921.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of organisational preparation from the later suspension of the campaign.
accepted.sec: ■ Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign - firka, district, leaders, tax refused  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary was known as Andhra Shivaji. Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was associated with the title Andhra Ratna, while Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary was called Kavi Raju.
accepted.tq: Match each personality with the exact title, watching for swapped titles.
accepted.sec: ■ Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign - firka, district, leaders, tax refused  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who wrote the autobiography *Na Jeevitha Katha*?
accepted.x: *Na Jeevitha Katha* is the autobiography associated with Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao.
accepted.tq: Test author–work association using nearby freedom-movement personalities as distractors.
accepted.sec: ■ Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign - firka, district, leaders, tax refused  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ketana was associated with the title Abhinava Dandi, not Andhra Ratna. Andhra Ratna was the title of Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped title by checking each personality–title pair.
accepted.sec: ■ Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign - firka, district, leaders, tax refused  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which British official attributed the village-officer resignations primarily to low pay and heavy workload?
accepted.x: Collector A. Gellatly attributed the resignations to low pay and workload. Revenue Board member L. T. Harris instead blamed the Congress.
accepted.tq: Distinguish officials by their posts and by the explanations they offered.
accepted.sec: ■ Government response - officials, arrests, withdrawal  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to the government response to the Pedanandipadu campaign, consider the following statements:
1. L. T. Harris was sent to Guntur after attributing the resignations to Congress influence.
2. Rutherford was deployed to deal with the situation.
3. Rutherford’s proposal to ban the Shanti Sena was accepted by the Madras Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Rutherford’s proposal to ban the Shanti Sena was rejected by the Madras Government, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-action trap: a proposed government measure was rejected, not accepted.
accepted.sec: ■ Government response - officials, arrests, withdrawal  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the Congress positions during the Pedanandipadu campaign?
o: Nyapathi Subbarao supported it; T. Prakasam urged its withdrawal
Rutherford and L. T. Harris supported it; Nyapathi Subbarao opposed it
Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri opposed it; Konda Venkatappayya urged restraint
Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri supported it; Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint
accepted.x: Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri backed the campaign, whereas Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint.
accepted.tq: Compare the positions of closely associated leaders rather than their official roles.
accepted.sec: ■ Government response - officials, arrests, withdrawal  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the inquiry committee that examined the Pedanandipadu campaign?
accepted.x: The inquiry committee consisted of T. Prakasam, Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao and Dantu Narayana Raju. Nyapathi Subbarao was not a member of this committee.
accepted.tq: Use the complete committee list and eliminate the nearby but unrelated name.
accepted.sec: ■ Government response - officials, arrests, withdrawal  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign was suspended after the Guntur District Congress Committee received Gandhi’s message to Konda Venkatappayya on:
accepted.x: Gandhi’s message to suspend the campaign reached the Guntur District Congress Committee on 11 February 1922, after which the campaign ended with the Non-Cooperation Movement.
accepted.tq: Match the precise date with the final administrative action in the campaign.
accepted.sec: ■ Government response - officials, arrests, withdrawal  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Delhi AICC meeting of 5 November 1921 permitted provincial committees to take up which activity?
o: Formation of provincial legislatures under the Government of India Act
accepted.x: The Delhi AICC permitted provincial committees to undertake civil disobedience, including no-tax campaigns. The Guntur campaign followed this decision.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise programme authorised by the national organisation.
accepted.sec: ■ Link with Bezawada AICC decisions and NCM programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bezawada AICC meeting of 1921 helped put Gandhi’s programme into Andhra.
2. The Chirala–Perala municipal tax struggle was a local version of the Non-Cooperation call.
3. The Palnadu forest satyagraha was unrelated to the Non-Cooperation programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Palnadu forest satyagraha was also a local expression of the same Non-Cooperation call, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed relationship in the statement describing a movement as unrelated.
accepted.sec: ■ Link with Bezawada AICC decisions and NCM programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following place–administrative unit pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chirala and Perala — Macherla taluka, Guntur district
Chirala and Perala — Bapatla taluka, Guntur district
accepted.x: Chirala and Perala belonged to Bapatla taluka of Guntur district. Palnadu was associated with Macherla in Guntur district, but Chirala and Perala were not in Macherla taluka.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related places by their taluka and district associations.
accepted.sec: ■ Place names - taluka and district  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Chirala and Perala, historically associated with the municipal tax struggle, are presently located in which district?
accepted.x: Chirala and Perala were formerly associated with Bapatla taluka of Guntur district and are now in Bapatla district.
accepted.tq: Track the distinction between the historical district and the present district.
accepted.sec: ■ Place names - taluka and district  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Madras Forest Act that affected the customary rights of tribal communities was enacted in:
accepted.x: The Madras Forest Act was enacted in 1882.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact year while separating the forest law from later rebellion dates.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Forest Act - year and provisions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a consequence of the Madras Forest Act, 1882, as described in relation to tribal grievances?
o: Recognition of unrestricted tribal access to minor forest produce
accepted.x: The Act restricted tribal access to podu cultivation and minor forest produce, and curbed grazing; it did not recognise unrestricted access.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that reverses the effect of a restrictive law.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Forest Act - year and provisions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The term ‘begar’ in the context of the tribal grievances in the Agency areas refers to:
o: A customary right to collect minor forest produce
A system of elected village councils
accepted.x: Begar meant forced unpaid labour, including work imposed on roads.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a labour practice and the separate forest and grazing grievances.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Forest Act - year and provisions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events of the Rampa rebellion in chronological order:
A. Raid on Annavaram Police Station
B. Attack on Chintapalli Police Station
C. Arrest of Gam Mallu Dora at Nadimpalem
D. Arrival of Assam Rifles and Gurkhas at Narsipatnam
accepted.x: Chintapalli was attacked on 22 August 1922, Annavaram was raided on 18 April 1923, Mallu Dora was arrested on 17 September 1923, and the Assam Rifles and Gurkhas reached Narsipatnam on 27 January 1924.
accepted.tq: Arrange events by anchoring the earliest police-station attack and the final military deployment.
accepted.sec: ■ Rampa rebellion chronology - start, police stations, end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 24 September 1922 — officers Scott Coward and Heiter killed at Damanapalli ghat
6 December 1922 — Gam Mallu Dora arrested at Nadimpalem
7 May 1924 — Gam Gantam Dora killed in firing
accepted.x: Scott Coward and Heiter were killed at Damanapalli ghat on 24 September 1922. Mallu Dora was arrested in September 1923, Raju was shot on 7 May 1924, and Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924.
accepted.tq: Match each event with its exact date and avoid swapping the final stages of the rebellion.
accepted.sec: ■ Rampa rebellion chronology - start, police stations, end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The first defeat suffered by Alluri Sitarama Raju’s forces at the hands of the Malabar Special Police occurred at:
accepted.x: At Peddagaddapalem on 6 December 1922, the Malabar Special Police inflicted Raju’s first defeat; he was wounded at Lingapuram.
accepted.tq: Separate the sites of the first defeat, the direct battle and the wounding.
accepted.sec: ■ Rampa rebellion chronology - start, police stations, end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Rampa rebellion extended approximately from:
accepted.x: The rebellion lasted from January 1922 to May 1924, approximately two years and five months, in the Agency tracts of East Godavari and Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Use the beginning and ending months together rather than relying only on the commonly remembered year range.
accepted.sec: ■ Rampa rebellion chronology - start, police stations, end  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following rebellions in chronological order:
A. Alluri Sitarama Raju’s Rampa rebellion
B. Vasudev Balwant Phadke’s revolt
C. Khudiram Bose’s Muzaffarpur episode
D. Gulugonda tribal revolt
accepted.x: The Gulugonda revolt occurred in 1845–48, Phadke’s revolt in 1879, Khudiram Bose’s episode in 1908, and Alluri’s Rampa rebellion in 1922–24.
accepted.tq: Place events by their periods before checking the sequence of the middle items.
accepted.sec: ■ Rebellions in chronological order - Phadke, Khudiram Bose, Alluri  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Gulugonda tribal revolt of 1845–48 was associated with which leader and region?
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju in the Gudem hills
accepted.x: The Gulugonda tribal revolt took place in the Vizag region during 1845–48 under Chinna Bhupathi.
accepted.tq: Match the regional rebellion with its specific leader and period.
accepted.sec: ■ Rebellions in chronological order - Phadke, Khudiram Bose, Alluri  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gam Gantam Dora — Lieutenant of Alluri
Gam Mallu Dora — Right hand of Alluri
Gam Mallu Dora — Killed on 7 June 1924
accepted.x: Gam Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924. Gam Mallu Dora was arrested in 1923, received a life term, was later released and won election as an MP in 1952.
accepted.tq: Detect the swapped fate and date among closely associated leaders.
accepted.sec: ■ Associates of Alluri - role  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who was arrested on 6 May 1924 at the Maddaru river?
accepted.x: Aggiraju was arrested at the Maddaru river on 6 May 1924.
accepted.tq: Link the arrest location and date to the correct associate rather than the British officer involved.
accepted.sec: ■ Associates of Alluri - role  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which British officer was appointed Special Commissioner to crush the Rampa rebellion?
accepted.x: Rutherford served as Special Commissioner to crush the revolt and ordered the exile of 55 helpers; warrants were issued for 183 persons.
accepted.tq: Match the officer with the specific administrative post and action.
accepted.sec: ■ British officers involved - post  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Raju was shot in the presence of which British officer?
accepted.x: Goodall was the Major in whose presence Alluri Sitarama Raju was shot.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the officer present at the execution from officers holding broader administrative or police roles.
accepted.sec: ■ British officers involved - post  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding British officers in the Rampa campaign is correct?
1. Bastian was the local Tahsildar whose excesses helped spark the rebellion.
2. Keirns arrested Gam Mallu Dora.
3. Scott Coward and Heiter were police officers killed at Damanapalli.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Bastian’s local excesses contributed to the grievance, Keirns arrested Mallu Dora, and Scott Coward and Heiter were killed at Damanapalli.
accepted.tq: Verify a group of officer–post or officer–event associations without swapping their roles.
accepted.sec: ■ British officers involved - post  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Agency tribes and their grievances:
1. Koya and other hill tribes were affected by the reservation of forests.
2. Forest restrictions curtailed podu, or shifting cultivation.
3. The Muttadari system was associated with extortion and forced labour.
4. Begar referred to voluntary paid labour on public roads.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Begar meant forced unpaid labour, not voluntary paid labour, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Identify the one reversed definition in a cluster of genuine tribal grievances.
accepted.sec: ■ Agency tribes and grievances - podu, muttadars, forced labour  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the connection between the Muttadari system and the Rampa rebellion?
o: It abolished the practice of podu cultivation.
It provided elected representation to hill tribes.
It involved extortion and forced labour imposed on tribal communities.
It guaranteed tribal access to reserved forests.
accepted.x: The Muttadari system generated resentment through extortion and forced labour, adding to the grievances caused by forest restrictions and begar.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional grievance to the social and economic causes of the rebellion.
accepted.sec: ■ Agency tribes and grievances - podu, muttadars, forced labour  [GROUP-II]
